newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market quiet, Brazil orders seen.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market quiet, Brazil orders seen.

text.p: Business was routine on the sugar freight market at the end of the week with only two new orders emerging for Brazilian ports, shipbrokers said on Friday.

Jean Lion fixed 12/13,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Continent to Dammam or Dubai for prompt dates and Booker was said to have covered 9/11,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Georgetown to UK/Nantes for October/November.
Details on the rates have yet to emerge.
CSR was said to have covered its order for 18/19,000 tonnes in bulk from Queensland to Japan for 10/20 November. Shipbrokers said the rate achieved was between $18 and $19.
Two new orders emerged for Brazilian origins.

Czarnikow Rionda quoted for 18,600 tonnes in bulk from Paranagua to Black Sea/Egyptian Mediterranean for mid-November dates and Cargill was open for 13,000 tonnes in bulk from north Brazil to Morocco/Egyptian Med/Black Sea options.
Elsewhere, the director-general of the Indian Sugar Mills Association said India hoped to export 500,000 tonnes of sugar to Pakistan in the 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) season.

Pakistan is expected to import about 700,000 tonnes of sugar in 1996/97, he said, adding that in 1995/96 Pakistan bought 400,000 tonnes of sugar out of which 350,000 tonnes were purchased from India. The balance would arrive from Brazil.
In another devlopment, the Commerce Minister said India was likely to decide soon on allowing fresh 500,000 tonnes of sugar for exports in 1996/97.
In June India authorised the food ministry to allow, in phases, export of one million tonnes of sugar in 1996/97.
